facts.fact: The Inter-Ministerial Committee on Migration said Home Affairs is expected to introduce a phased online intention-registration and appointment system for asylum applicants by 10 November 2026, issuing a receipt recording personal particulars, biometrics, a reference number and an appointment.

facts.fact: Minister Leon Schreiber said Home Affairs is developing a biometric online platform for asylum applications, expected to be operational by 10 November 2026, requiring applicants to submit biometrics to verify identity and detect earlier rejected claims.
EWN reported that Home Affairs plans to introduce a digital asylum registration and appointment system by 10 November 2026.

facts.fact: Home Affairs says its portal to record asylum seekers' intention to apply, with facial biometrics and documents, is live for test cases; it confers no status and is not a formal application.

South Africa's Home Affairs has begun testing a digital asylum system in which people register an intention to apply for asylum with facial biometrics, biographic data and documents, which is not yet a formal application or status.
The Minister of Home Affairs reported 57,288 refugees with active section 24 permits under the Refugees Act and 80,803 asylum seekers with active section 22 permits.
The Minister of Home Affairs' reply lists active permits at 31 December 2024 by country of origin, which sum to 92,657 section 22 asylum seeker permits and 62,649 section 24 refugee permits.

note: Refugee services are mentioned only as a function affected by outages; no registration or digital access stated.
